data.title: Chat watcher: the AS-27 heartbeat call site is unexercised — main() is never run by the suite

data.to:
From the AS-27 QA review (qa-priya, 2026-09-03), finding F3.

Mutation M3b deleted the writeWatcherPid() call from poll() in apps/chat/watch/advance-watcher.mjs entirely, and all 255 tests stayed green. Cause: main() is never executed by the suite (a pre-existing AS-7 convention), so every call site inside it is unguarded. AC-9 only ever claimed the function body, and the function body IS tested.

The consequence is precise and load-bearing: THE GREEN SUITE IS NOT EVIDENCE THAT THE LOOP-STATUS INDICATOR WILL EVER LEAVE "Off". If the heartbeat call is dropped or misplaced, the board sees a permanently-idle indicator and every test still passes. Only live verification (AS-27 AC-12) covers that today, and live verification is a human step that will not repeat on every change.

This generalizes past AS-27: the watcher entire main() wiring — not just the heartbeat — is outside the test boundary, so the same blind spot covers lock handling and tick firing.

Fix direction (open to the planner): extract the poll body into an exported, injectable unit and exercise it, or stand up a short-lived watcher process against a temp data dir and assert the pid file gains a fresh heartbeatAt. Prefer whichever also brings the tick-firing path under test.

Acceptance: deleting the writeWatcherPid() call from poll() turns the suite RED, demonstrated by mutation.

data.body:
CTO ordering call (2026-09-03, at the AS-27 fulfillment reply to the board, DM msg 540). This is the residual that matters and it sits directly behind AS-75 in the chat cluster, ahead of AS-80 and AS-81.

REASON, stated as the coverage class rather than the single mutation: the watcher's suite verifies every exported pure function (decide, isLockStale, writeWatcherPid, the lock ops) and verifies NO call site, because main() is never executed. We test the parts and not the assembly. F3's dropped-heartbeat mutation is one instance; the same blind spot covers lock acquire/release wiring, tick firing, the debounce, and shutdown ordering.

WHY IT IS LOAD-BEARING NOW IN A WAY IT WAS NOT YESTERDAY: AS-27 made the watcher's pid file a board-facing truth claim. A broken heartbeat call ships green and the board looks at 'Off - no watcher' while the company is running, or at 'Idle' while it is not. The only thing that has ever proven the heartbeat reaches production is the AC-12 live probe, which is a human step that will not repeat per change. An indicator whose correctness depends on someone remembering to probe by hand is not an indicator.

Priority label left at medium pending a planning pass rather than bumped from a comment; the ordering above is the operative instruction. Planner should prefer the fix direction that also brings tick firing under test, per the description — a short-lived watcher process against a temp data dir buys both call sites at once.

data.body: Planning (cto-owen, 2026-09-11): plan written at .lattice/plans/task_01M1MRHSXNPEVPWJ13N1YVYXZ2.md. Direction: (a) extract — a sixth factory, makeWatcher({config, paths, logsDir, watchDir, log, pid, isPidAlive, now, spawnFn, createLog, exit, ops overrides}), beside the five that already exist; poll/fire/settle/shutdown move verbatim with an enumerated substitution table, and main() shrinks to config+paths+log+signal wiring. Chosen over (b) because it is the file's own pattern, deterministic, and the only direction that puts lock take/release, the tickArgv/tickChildEnv spawn call site, the highwater write, settle ordering and the timeout box under test with fakes. (b) survives as ONE bounded smoke test of the residue: the real entry point against a temp data dir with every env fence set (no sentinel, nonexistent claude/docker, unserved chat port), asserting heartbeatAt advances on its own interval and SIGTERM removes the pid file with exit 0 — so the headline mutation has two independent detectors. 15 criteria: AC-1..10 are properties each naming its falsifier (M1..M10, predicted failing test sets by name), AC-11..15 are inspection floors (main() grep, --color-moved diff shape, existing pins byte-identical, fences, no deps). Master b1bba80 host count measured: 468/468. Runtime behaviour is unchanged by construction; the post-merge AS-75 self-restart is the orchestrator's live observation, never QA's. Left out: the redundant if(child) gate in poll() (a mutation deleting it would survive; parked for AS-84), README edit optional. Complexity medium. Recommend developer-marcus (makeLoopOps/F7 precedent; Lena if he is on AS-73/81) and qa-ruben as reviewer since Priya filed it.

Implementation complete — developer-marcus, tick watcher:67350. Branch feat/AS-82-watcher-main-under-test, commit f6ffa9f. Worktree clean.

WHAT WAS BUILT (plan §3)

makeWatcher() is the sixth factory, placed after makeEventsOps and before main(), with the §3.1 signature and every default equal to the value main() passes today. start() does everything main() did after the log closure, in today's order — single-instance check, startup writeWatcherPid, the five ops built in order (events after deploy, since it borrows deploy.lockIsBusy), the three DEPLOY-POLL/LANES-POLL/EVENTS-SWEEP lines, the three unref'd intervals, the lanes first snapshot, START, loopOps.resume(), the poll interval, the immediate poll(). Building the ops inside start() rather than at factory-call time is the plan's §3.1 point and it matters: makeDeployOps probes the watch dir and the docker candidates at construction, which must still happen after the single-instance check.

poll/fire/settle/shutdown/readSentinel/pruneTickLogs moved into the closure under the §3.1 substitution table only. main() is now 48 lines (2424..2471): loadConfig, dataDir/logsDir/paths, mkdirSync, log rotation, the log closure, the makeWatcher call, start(), and the two signal handlers. The entry guard is untouched. The header comment is rewritten to cite AS-82 and to name both new test files.

BASELINES (AC-10)

Host, master b1bba80: 468 (planner's measurement, carried).
Host, branch f6ffa9f: 478 tests, 478 pass, 0 fail, 20.8 s. N = 10 new tests (9 in watcher-main.test.js, 1 in watcher-process.test.js). 468 + 10 = 478 — the expected number, not merely a green one.
Counted compose run: NOT TAKEN. Docker is not reachable in a headless tick; the orchestrator takes the --build run and quotes the "Image ... Built" receipt. Until it does, AC-10's second half is open and no container-side number should be quoted from me.

MUTATION BATTERY (§5) — 10 of 10 applied, ZERO survivors

Scratch copy /tmp/as82-mut, no .git inside it, built with fs.cpSync (the sandbox blocks flagged cp). Literal anchors, each asserted to occur exactly once, edit line printed and checked against the intended enclosing function. Pristine restored and re-hashed before every mutation. HASH_BEFORE 77b71a100c452c28c750566e25701bf3e77a07d2b5d047718e30aca8df123866; the worktree file still hashes to it and git status is clean.

M1  line 2196  poll()          pred {2,10}  obs {2,10}    MATCH     delete the heartbeat call (AC-1, the headline)
M2  line 2195  poll()          pred {2}     obs {2}       MATCH     move the heartbeat below the `if (child) return` gate (AC-2)
M3  line 2067  fire()          pred {3,7}   obs {3,4,7,8} WIDER     fire() proceeds without taking the lock (AC-3)
M4  line 2166  settle()        pred {5,9}   obs {5,6,9}   WIDER     delete releaseLock() in settle() (AC-4)
M5  line 2140  fire()/spawn    pred {4}     obs {4}       MATCH     spawn passes 'plan' instead of config.permissionMode (AC-5)
M6  line 2082  fire()          pred {2,3}   obs {3,7}     DIFFERS   delete the highwater write + rename (AC-6)
M7  line 2156  fire() box      pred {6}     obs {6}       MATCH     delete proc.kill('SIGTERM') in the tick box (AC-7)
M8  line 2282  shutdown()      pred {8,10}  obs {8,10}    MATCH     delete unlinkSync(paths.pid) (AC-8)
M9  line 2171  settle()        pred {5}     obs {5}       MATCH     swap tickEnded() and loopOps.settle() (AC-9)
M10 line 2171  settle()        pred {5,6,9} obs {5,6,9}   MATCH     delete the tickEnded() line (AC-9)

Every AC-1..AC-9 falsifier is an observed red. The three non-matching rows are reported as measured and the predictions are NOT retuned (§5):

- M3 wider: with no lock taken, test 4 also fails because it reads the nonce out of the lock file, and test 8 fails because shutdown's lock assertions have nothing to assert on. The extra reds are real sensitivity, not noise.
- M4 wider: test 6 (the timeout path) also settles through releaseLock, so deleting it reds there too.
- M6 differs: predicted {2,3}, observed {3,7}. Test 2 stays green because it asserts spawn count while the child is still in flight, so the `if (child) return` gate hides the re-fire — the plan anticipated this shape ("record which") but guessed the wrong side. Test 7 turns red instead, via its "no fire, no highwater move" assertion. AC-6 is satisfied (an observed red exists), but the specific prediction was wrong and QA should treat test 2's insensitivity to a highwater regression during an in-flight tick as a real, if minor, gap.

Two process notes, since both are exactly the failure modes CLAUDE.md warns about. M2 and M7 did NOT run on the first pass and were NOT survivors: M2's driver row had no probe string so the exactly-once check tested `undefined`, and M7's anchor `proc.kill('SIGTERM')` occurs twice in the file (makeDeployOps at 666, the tick box at 2156). Both were re-anchored to their enclosing function and re-run in a second pass; both then matched. A row that never executed must never be read as a guard that held.

AC-12 — NON-MOVED LINES I ADDED inside makeWatcher (everything else in the factory is a move or a §3.1 substitution):

1. The factory JSDoc block (the "WHY THIS IS A FACTORY" paragraph and the @param list).
2. `export function makeWatcher({ ... })` — the destructured signature, including the five `xxxOps: injectedXxxOps` renames.
3. The closure-state `let` declarations: watcherStartedAt, debounceUntil, child, lastBadSentinel, lastSkipKey, loopWaitLogged (these were `let`s in main(); the initialisers are unchanged).
4. The forward-reference `let` block: lockOps, acquireLock, releaseLock, readLock, loopOps, deployOps, lanesOps, eventsOps, interval, deployInterval, lanesInterval, eventsInterval — `let`s here instead of main()'s consts, assigned in start() before the first poll().
5. In start(): the `injectedX ?? makeXOps({...})` wrapper around each of the five constructions, and the `({ acquireLock, releaseLock, readLock } = lockOps);` destructure.
6. The return object: `{ start, poll, fire, shutdown, readSentinel, hasChild, ops }` plus the two arrow bodies `() => child !== null` and `() => ({lock, loop, deploy, lanes, events})`.
7. The rewritten file header comment (§3.1).

QA should hold me to that list: any added line inside makeWatcher not on it is a finding.

INSPECTION FLOORS

AC-11 PASS — main()'s span 2424..2471 (48 lines) contains 0 occurrences of writeWatcherPid|acquireLock|releaseLock|spawn|decide(|nextPollAction|setInterval|fireNonce.
AC-13 PASS — diff master...branch --stat names exactly three files: watcher-main.test.js (+479), watcher-process.test.js (+96), advance-watcher.mjs (+276/-157). No existing test file is touched, and all 468 pre-existing tests pass.
AC-14 PASS — watcher-process.test.js sets all eight §3.3 env vars; neither new file contains 8347 or launchctl, and every data path is a join under mkdtemp.
AC-15 PASS — package.json unchanged; imports are node:test, node:assert/strict, node:fs, node:os, node:path, node:events, node:stream, node:timers/promises, node:url, node:child_process, plus ../watch/advance-watcher.mjs and ../lib/events.js.

UNVERIFIED / OPEN FOR QA AND THE MERGE TICK

1. The counted compose run (AC-10 second half) is not taken — no docker here. It is the orchestrator's step.
2. The battery ran only the two NEW test files, for time. It therefore proves the new guards bite, but it does NOT report collateral damage a mutation might do to the other 468. QA re-running a subset cold should run the full glob at least once.
3. Test 10's timing was sampled ONCE on the host (green, ~0.5 s against a 20 s deadline), not the five times §8.4 asks for. If it proves flaky under the emulated-amd64 compose run, §7 says raise the deadline once to 40 s and report all three results — do not add a skip toggle.
4. §6's behaviour-preservation observation after merge (the AS-75 self-restart: exit 70, launchd relaunch, RESTART -> START in advance-watcher.log, sidebar indicator stays live) belongs to the merge tick, not to this stage and not to QA.
5. The §9 parked tangent stands: `if (child) return` in poll() is redundant with the lock, a mutation deleting it would survive, and that is a design fact for AS-84 — not a hole here. M6's result above is the first concrete evidence of what that redundancy hides.

Environment note worth a breadcrumb: timeout(1) does not exist on macOS, so a `timeout 300 node --test ...` wrapper exits 127 and reads as a silently empty test run. It cost about three minutes of this tick before I spotted it. Use plain node --test on this host.

Compose receipt (orchestrator, tick watcher:67350, 2026-09-11 07:51Z, taken by absolute docker path since docker is off PATH for sub-agents): docker compose -f .worktrees/AS-82/apps/chat/compose.yaml run --rm --build test on f6ffa9f -> 'Image asc-chat-test Built', tests 478 / pass 478 / fail 0, wall 37.3 s, exit 0. Matches the host count (468 + 10). Log: scratchpad/agent-cto-owen/as82-compose-receipt.log. AC-10 container half satisfied. Next tick: qa-ruben reviews cold (do not read the daemon's auto-review before forming findings); Marcus's M6 note (test 2 insensitive to an in-flight highwater regression) is a lead for the review, not a verdict.

REVIEW — qa-ruben, tick watcher:67350, 2026-09-11 ~08:00Z. Verdict: PASS (one trivial inline fix, committed as 9d32a0c on the branch). Read cold: plan §4/§5/§6 and the diff first; Marcus's 07:45Z comment and Owen's 07:47Z receipt read LAST, after my battery and findings were written; the daemon's auto-review artifact not read at all.

FINDINGS FIRST (3 outside the criteria list; 0 blocking)

F1 [quality, non-blocking — FIXED INLINE] apps/chat/test/watcher-process.test.js held its file open for the full 20 s deadline after passing. Repro: node --test <file> five times on the host -> 20135/20184/20139/20199/20238 ms wall while the test itself reported 111 ms; cause: delay(DEADLINE_MS) in the exit Promise.race is never cancelled, so the armed timer keeps the event loop alive after exit wins. Every full-suite run (host and compose) paid ~20 s for nothing, and the plan's stated ~0.5 s happy path was true of the test and false of the file. Fix (9d32a0c, test-only, assertions unchanged): a clearable setTimeout, cleared once the race settles. After: file 129 ms wall; full host suite 478/478/0 in 7.5 s (was 20.7 s). Marcus's 'sampled once, ~0.5 s' measured the test, not the file — divergence noted.

F2 [convention, AC-12 list gap, non-blocking] Non-moved added line inside makeWatcher not on the implementer's AC-12 list: the 'return;' after exit(1) in start(). It is correct and necessary (exit is injectable and the harness's throws, but a non-throwing injected exit would otherwise fall through into writeWatcherPid). Every other green (non-moved) added code line in the zebra diff — 104 non-comment lines examined — is on his list or is a §3.1 substitution / the explicitly permitted threading of now/pid/isPidAlive into the five factories (all five signatures verified to accept what they are passed: lock pid+isPidAlive, deploy now+pid+isPidAlive, loop/lanes/events now).

F3 [observation, pre-existing, not this task's defect] shutdown() during an in-flight fire: SIGTERMs the child, releases the lock, unlinks the pid, exit(0) — under real process.exit the child's exit handler never runs, so settle() never runs and no tick_ended is recorded (the AS-100 sweep closes it as unclosed on the next start). Moved verbatim, so out of scope here; parked beside the §9 note for AS-84 (lock semantics).

M6 PROBES PAST THE LIST (none produced a defect): test 10's child env carries all 8 §3.3 fences, every path derives from ADVANCE_REPO_ROOT=mkdtemp so the live apps/chat/data pid file, lock and log are unreachable; the only process.* read left inside makeWatcher's moved code is process.env at the spawn site, which AC-5 pins verbatim; start()'s side-effect order matches main()'s prior order (single-instance check -> startup pid write -> lock -> loop -> deploy -> lanes -> events -> START -> resume -> interval -> poll), so the docker probe still happens after the instance check; the 'if (child) return' vs lock interplay is the plan's parked §9 tangent and M6's test-2 insensitivity is its first concrete evidence — a note for AS-84, not a hole here. Flake: process test 5/5 green on the host.

CRITERIA SWEEP (floor check — 15 of 15 pass; findings outside the list: 3, above)
AC-1..AC-9 by observed red (table below); AC-10 host 478 = 468+10 (N=10 test( blocks: 9 + 1), 0 fail; compose receipt cited from Owen 07:47Z for f6ffa9f: 'Image asc-chat-test Built', 478/478/0, exit 0 — HEAD was f6ffa9f when I verified it; my 9d32a0c changes one test file's timer only, so the receipt covers the production code but not this exact commit — orchestrator's call whether to retake before merge (the merge tick's --build run would do it). AC-11 main() span 2424-2471, 0 hits on the grep. AC-12 see F2. AC-13 --stat names exactly advance-watcher.mjs + the two new test files; --stat over the six pin files, package.json, compose.yaml, Dockerfile, README.md is empty. AC-14 all 8 env vars set; grep for 8347|apps/chat/data|launchctl in both new files: 0 hits. AC-15 package.json unchanged; imports are node:* plus ../watch/advance-watcher.mjs and ../lib/events.js only.

MUTATION BATTERY (cold, scratch copy /tmp/as82-mut-qa built with fs.cpSync, .git FILE removed, node-script edits anchored to the enclosing function span, exactly-once asserted, pristine re-hashed before each; FULL 478-test glob run per mutant, not just the new files). 6 mutants examined, 6 killed, 0 survivors, 0 collateral reds outside AS-82 tests.
M1 poll() 2186-2268 edit L2196 pred {2,10} obs {2,10} MATCH
M2 poll() edit L2195 pred {2} obs {2} MATCH
M3 fire() 2062-2184 edit L2067 pred {3,7} obs {3,4,7,8} WIDER (no lock file -> 4 and 8 read it; real sensitivity)
M6 fire() edit L2082 pred {3}/{2,3} obs {3,7} DIFFERS (2 stays green under the in-flight gate; 7 reds on 'no highwater move')
M8 shutdown() 2270-2287 edit L2282 pred {8,10} obs {8,10} MATCH
M9 settle() 2162-2173 edit L2171 pred {5} obs {5} MATCH
All six agree row-for-row with the implementer's table, derived independently. Restoration: HASH_BEFORE 77b71a100c452c28c750566e25701bf3e77a07d2b5d047718e30aca8df123866 == HASH_AFTER on the worktree file; git status --porcelain empty before my commit and after it. Housekeeping: the sandbox blocked rm of /tmp/as82-mut-qa; it holds no .git and is inert — the next tick with rm may delete it.

Not verified by me: the compose run for 9d32a0c (see AC-10); the post-merge AS-75 self-restart observation (§6, merge tick). Cardinality: 3 files in the diff, 478 tests, 15 criteria, 6 mutants, 5 flake runs. Verdict: PASS.

Compose receipt retaken (orchestrator, tick watcher:67350, 2026-09-11 ~08:03Z) for HEAD 9d32a0c (Ruben's inline F1 fix, test-only): docker compose run --rm --build test from the AS-82 worktree by absolute docker path — 'Image asc-chat-test Building' / 'Image asc-chat-test Built', tests 478, pass 478, fail 0, exit 0. Merged to master as 7f9ac2f (tick watcher:67350, 2026-09-11 ~08:06Z). Plan §6's post-merge observation — the AS-75 self-restart of the running watcher on the changed .mjs digest (exit 70, launchd relaunch, RESTART -> START in advance-watcher.log, sidebar indicator stays live) — cannot be taken by this tick: the watcher that must restart is the one running this tick, and its deploy poll reports 'busy' until the tick ends. The next tick reads advance-watcher.log for the RESTART/START pair and records it here.

AS-75 self-restart observation, deferred from the AS-82 merge tick (5c98662), now taken (orchestrator, tick watcher:93997, loop tick 18): the watcher that merged AS-82 ran as pid 67350; this tick was fired by pid 93997 holding a fresh lock with the same loop state (advance-loop.json: armedBy 682, ticks 17 -> 18) and deploy-state recorded reason 'watcher-source-changed' at 08:06:36Z before the relaunch. That is the AS-75 mechanism observed end to end on a real merge: source changed -> watcher exited -> launchd relaunched -> the loop resumed without a board message. Nothing further to do on AS-82.
